comments.text: In no way suggesting this did or didn't happen to any of the 'blink and they are gone' kids but I did come across a video on how people can disappear very very easily even in open spaces let alone woods. You could walk literally a foot from it and you wouldn't see it. It was found by a fluke - searcher stepped in it I believe - and the body was at the bottom of it. Another was a man who was crushed by a slab of rock that dislodged from a small cliff. 31:35 .. I’m “old” now.. 
but as a relatively unusual kid, I started out learning wilderness survival as a very young girl, so I’d been taught survival shelter building before I was even in 3d grade.. I spent countless hours in the woods as a free range GenX kid, I had a very solid background in outdoor/bushcraft life my entire childhood..
Even with that, I got “lost” from a heavily traveled trail in a state park in upstate NY in the mid 80s.. 
..one minute I’m skipping along ahead of the family pack, next thing I realize, I’m definitely NOT on the “trail” anymore..
I had enough experience and logical thinking skills by that age, to realize how I’d gotten sidetracked off trail and was able to retrace my steps and get back to the “real trail”, I was flustered and anxious, but I found my way back and was coping..
..my dad??? OMFG.. not coping..
To their eyes, I’d just VANISHED..
I went around the bend a little bit ahead and disappeared.. they went all the way to the top of the mountain looking and my dad was in a PANIC by the time they found me on the way to call the police..

I KNOW how people can just 💨 POOF! I did it.. and it’s a LOT easier than you’d think.. if a younger kid, or someone without experience, or just bad circumstances, gets off trail, they can very easily end up MILES away from where they were and where someone would “think” they’d end up.. 
and in the north east, and places like it, if there’s not bulky equipment, plastics, metals, bright colors of gear.. someone can disappear FOREVER and never be found, all it takes is one summer, fall and winter and anything left is buried in leaves and debris and just gets more and more buried every year..
..the woods are no joke.. 

My heart breaks for the families and friends of stories like this.. I always hope that they get answers someday..

I’m still a bushcrafter/camper decades later, but I have an extremely healthy respect for the environment and have lots of plans for any kind of incident that might occur out there..
